newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to raise prices on controlled foods - radio.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to raise prices on controlled foods - radio.

text.p: Mexico's government is to raise controlled prices of corn pancake tortillas and pasteurised milk, national radio network Radio Red said Thursday.
Citing a communique from the Trade Ministry, the radio said tortillas will go up to 1.70 peso per kilo from 1.40 peso and milk will increase to 4.00 pesos per liter from 3.60 pesos.

Radio Red said the price hikes will be announced in the government's Official Gazette on Friday. But it did not specify when they would come into effect. It could be from the date of publication or from Janaury 1.
A spokeswoman from the Trade Ministry told Reuters she was not aware of any communique announcing the hikes in prices.
Farm sector leaders have pushed for increases, and in some cases of a total freeing up of controls on prices, for months, arguing they were losing money.

The hikes will have an impact on inflation because both foodstuffs are important elements of the consumer price index and also of the basic basket of goods. They are among a handful of foods that are still price controlled in Mexico to make sure poor citizens have access to foods.
